---
title: "Estimation with time aggregation"
---

Bansal, Kiku, and Yaron (2016) estimate the long-run risks model by
GMM, jointly with the decision frequency $h$. Latent expected-growth
and volatility states come from the price-dividend ratio and the
risk-free rate. The sample is annual, 1930 to 2015, from the paper's
sources: CRSP value-weighted NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ, BLS CPI, the 90-day
T-bill, and BEA NIPA consumption.

This page holds Tables 1 to 3 and Figure 1. [Time
aggregation](time-aggregation.qmd) holds Tables 4 to 6 and Figure 2,
[Size and book-to-market claims](portfolios.qmd) holds Table 7, and
[Post-war quarterly data](quarterly.qmd) holds Table 8. In every table
the column marked "paper" is the paper's printed value, and the column
beside it is computed by the cell above the table.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
from great_tables import GT

from geap.lrr.estimation import (
    TABLE_3_LRR_MODEL,
    TABLE_3_LRR_RESIDUALS,
    TABLE_3_NOVOL_MODEL,
    TABLE_3_NOVOL_RESIDUALS,
    estimate_bky,
    figure1_frame,
    figure1_ggplot,
    load_annual,
    long_run_variance_share,
    table1_frame,
    table2_frame,
    table3_compare,
)

KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem",
               heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem",
               source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold",
               data_row_padding="4px")


def fmt_params(gt, tab):
    """Two decimals for the large parameters, four for the rest, scientific for sigma_w."""
    idx = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(tab["parameter"])}
    two = [idx[n] for n in ("gamma", "psi", "phi_d", "phi_d_sigma", "h", "J") if n in idx]
    three = [idx[n] for n in ("rho_d", "p") if n in idx]
    sci = [idx[n] for n in ("sigma_w",) if n in idx]
    four = [i for i in range(len(tab)) if i not in two + three + sci]
    num = [c for c in tab.columns if c != "parameter"]
    return (
        gt.fmt_number(columns=num, rows=four, decimals=4)
        .fmt_number(columns=num, rows=two, decimals=2)
        .fmt_number(columns=num, rows=three, decimals=3)
        .fmt_scientific(columns=num, rows=sci, decimals=2)
        .sub_missing(missing_text="")
    )


def fmt_moments(gt, tab):
    idx = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(tab["moment"])}
    sci = [idx[n] for n in ("e_eta_x", "e_eta2_s2") if n in idx]
    rest = [i for i in range(len(tab)) if i not in sci]
    num = [c for c in tab.columns if c != "moment"]
    levels = [c for c in num if not c.startswith("t_diff")]
    tstats = [c for c in num if c.startswith("t_diff")]
    gt = gt.fmt_number(columns=num, rows=rest, decimals=3)
    gt = gt.fmt_scientific(columns=levels, rows=sci, decimals=1)
    if tstats:
        gt = gt.fmt_number(columns=tstats, rows=sci, decimals=3)
    return gt.sub_missing(missing_text="")


panel = load_annual()
```

## Table 1: the sample

```{python}
tab1 = table1_frame(panel)
(
    GT(tab1)
    .tab_header(title="Table 1. Summary statistics, annual 1930 to 2015")
    .tab_spanner(label="Mean", columns=["ours_mean", "paper_mean"])
    .tab_spanner(label="Std. dev.", columns=["ours_sd", "paper_sd"])
    .cols_label(series="", ours_mean="ours", paper_mean="paper",
                ours_sd="ours", paper_sd="paper")
    .fmt_number(columns=["ours_mean", "paper_mean", "ours_sd", "paper_sd"], decimals=3)
    .tab_source_note("Ours: the shipped panel from CRSP, BLS, and BEA. Paper: BKY (2016) Table 1.")
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

## Table 2: GMM estimates

The LRR model is estimated with $h$ chosen on the grid 8 to 14 decisions
a year. The No-Vol model shuts the volatility state off, so $\nu$ and
$\sigma_w$ have no row. Standard errors next to our estimates are this
sample's sandwich SEs. The paper's are an eight-year block bootstrap.
The No-Vol surface has more than one basin, so that fit keeps the
lowest objective of several starts.

```{python}
fit = estimate_bky(panel)
novol = estimate_bky(panel, stochastic_vol=False, n_starts=3)
tab2 = table2_frame(fit, novol)
fmt_params(
    GT(tab2)
    .tab_header(title="Table 2. Model estimates: parameters")
    .tab_spanner(label="LRR model", columns=["lrr_hat", "lrr_se", "lrr_paper", "lrr_paper_se"])
    .tab_spanner(label="No-Vol model", columns=["novol_hat", "novol_se", "novol_paper", "novol_paper_se"])
    .cols_label(parameter="", lrr_hat="estimate", lrr_se="SE", lrr_paper="paper", lrr_paper_se="paper SE",
                novol_hat="estimate", novol_se="SE", novol_paper="paper", novol_paper_se="paper SE")
    .tab_source_note("J is Hansen's test of the overidentifying restrictions with its p-value. Paper: BKY (2016) Table 2."),
    tab2,
).tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
```

## Table 3: moments

Sample moments of the shipped panel, the model's implied moments at the
estimates, the $t$-statistic of the difference, and the paper's model
column. The six residual rows are the orthogonality restrictions on the
innovations to consumption and dividends after the states are
extracted.

```{python}
lrr3 = table3_compare(panel, fit, {**TABLE_3_LRR_MODEL, **TABLE_3_LRR_RESIDUALS})
nv3 = table3_compare(panel, novol, {**TABLE_3_NOVOL_MODEL, **TABLE_3_NOVOL_RESIDUALS})
tab3 = lrr3.merge(nv3.drop(columns="sample"), on="moment", suffixes=("_lrr", "_novol"))
fmt_moments(
    GT(tab3)
    .tab_header(title="Table 3. Model estimates: moments")
    .tab_spanner(label="LRR model", columns=["model_lrr", "t_diff_lrr", "paper_model_lrr"])
    .tab_spanner(label="No-Vol model", columns=["model_novol", "t_diff_novol", "paper_model_novol"])
    .cols_label(moment="", sample="sample", model_lrr="model", t_diff_lrr="t(diff)", paper_model_lrr="paper",
                model_novol="model", t_diff_novol="t(diff)", paper_model_novol="paper")
    .tab_source_note("Sample and model columns are ours at the Table 2 estimates. Paper: BKY (2016) Table 3 model columns."),
    tab3,
).tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
```

```{python}
print(f"long-run share of var(dc) at the LRR estimates: {long_run_variance_share(fit.params, fit.h):.2f}")
```

`estimate_bky` takes the panel and a Bansal and Yaron (2004) monthly
start. Integer $h$ is chosen on a grid. `n_boot` replaces the sandwich
SEs with an eight-year moving-block bootstrap, `bootstrap_h=True`
re-selects $h$ on each draw, and `n_starts` runs the CUE from several
spread-out starts and keeps the lowest objective.

::: {.firewall}
Every "paper" column is quoted from Bansal, Kiku, and Yaron (2016),
Tables 1 to 3. Everything else on this page is computed by the cell
above it from the shipped 1930 to 2015 panel. Market return, dividend
growth, and log P/D match Table 1 to display precision. NIPA revisions
move mean consumption growth down by about 0.17 percentage points, and
the fitted ex-ante T-bill sits about 19 basis points above the printed
0.5 percent; `tests/test_bky_goldens.py` locks those gaps. The No-Vol
estimates do not land on the paper's: the CUE surface under that
restriction is flat in the IES, pushes persistence to its bound, and
doubles the dividend loading, and the fit reports the lowest objective
of its three starts. `NUMBERS.md` lists the open caveats.
:::
